proposal.claim:
Origin, stated first. This is NOT from reports/SCOUT.jsonl, and the reason is the evaluator rather than the notebook. Eighteen payers are in it now. Twelve are anchored to a clock or an announcement -- the quarterly 07:00-08:00 UTC delivery fixing on the last Friday of a quarter, the Deribit expiry and Dual Investment 07:30-08:00 windows, the CME 15:00-16:00 London hour, the Monday 00:00 UTC liquidity-provider tier reset, the daily 00:00 UTC tournament qualification reset, the pre-announced margin-tier change, the jurisdiction offboarding deadlines, the BUSD collateral wind-down, the delisting settlement -- and no field of TrialConfig or SignalTrialConfig can name a date, an hour or a weekday, while a Track A programme is anchored only to its own start offset and the evaluator enumerates EVERY offset, so a percentile taken across them averages a fixing hour away by construction. Five more -- forced short covering, short-gamma delta hedging, leveraged-token rebalancing, copy-trade replication, TWAP child orders -- need an intrabar forced-flow proxy, and H0008 and H0009 both died discovering that this vocabulary has none. The venue-outage line says outright that its observable is the only one measurable entirely from the held panel, and it is right, but "bars missing simultaneously across the cross-section" is data forensics, not a rule any config field can express, and its honest home is a scout or robustness pass at zero ledger rows. This reading is not new and is not being re-derived to fill space: H0011 and H0012 both made it and neither adversary disputed it.

The closest notebook line to the shape below is the Binance Leveraged Token hedge basket that must trade WITH the move to restore a mandated leverage. It is the only payer in the notebook whose payment is triggered by a price state rather than by a clock or an order-book event, which is the one class this vocabulary can name at all. But its rebalance is a matter of minutes and the gate below is an average over weeks on a 1h clock, so this proposal does NOT claim to test it, and says so here rather than borrowing its language later. That borrowing is exactly what killed H0008: "a forced-cover mechanism attached only in prose".

Who is structurally paying, and why they keep doing it. Two receivers, and both matter. (1) The funding counterparty, who collects rent on notional every eight hours with no termination date -- that absence of a date is the whole product difference from a dated future. KT-1 put the rate at 87% of BTCUSDT settlements positive and a median bill of 36% of contributed capital over three years; the off-ledger measurement recorded in configs/killed/H0012.json puts DOGEUSDT's bill at 356% of contributed capital on a 1092-day funded weekly ladder. (2) At the maintenance boundary, the liquidation engine's counterparty and the insurance fund, because the engine sells at market inside the bar with no price discretion and charges a clearance fee. The payer is the perpetual accumulator, and it keeps standing there because the rent is levied on NOTIONAL while survival is set by MARGIN, and margin posted in excess of notional earns nothing at all -- so a holder who wants the exposure has a standing incentive to under-post, and the perpetual is the only continuously available levered long on this venue. Both adversaries accepted this payer as structural when H0012 named it (payer_is_structural true). H0012 died on its rule shape, not on its payer.

The new evidence, which did not exist when the last four proposals were reviewed. That same verdict measured liquidation_rate on the funded, unlevered, ungated weekly ladder at exactly the shape fixed below: BTCUSDT 0.570, ETHUSDT 0.484, BNBUSDT 0.000, DOGEUSDT 0.800, XRPUSDT 0.724, ADAUSDT 0.933 -- and 0.000 on every one of them with the funding leg switched off. The rent alone ruins the accumulator on five of six symbols. No Track A family has ever been read for that, and no Track A row has ever carried a rule that could act on it: across 1232 H0001 trials and 1332 Track A trials in total, the accumulator deploys every dollar on schedule and holds every coin to the terminal bar. So this hypothesis does not spend a single row asking whether the ruin is there. That is the premise, it is already measured at zero cost, and no clause below tests it -- which is the specific defect that killed H0012, where five of six clauses resolved to "survives" before registration.

What the rule shape is, and why it is not a field-move. Rent is charged on notional TIMES time. KT-1 measured the rate. H0012 asked about the ratio of notional to margin and was killed as a leverage sweep on H0001's shape. This asks about the BASE, using the only two controls the vocabulary has: a gate that leaves money undeployed in the middle of the programme, and an account-level abandonment that ends the exposure before the engine does.

The gate is `sma:<days>`, the one gate form with zero rows in this project and the opposite sign to every gate ever run here. H0007's dip gates bought weakness, and its surface reading concluded that a dip gate cannot change the price process -- it only re-orders which bars are bought inside the same decline, which is why H0009 was killed as a third threshold pair on that axis. A trend-state gate makes a different claim: that the stretches not worth holding notional through are identifiable from the asset's own trend rather than from its drawdown. It is also the only form in this vocabulary under which money sits in cash for extended stretches, so it is the only one that changes notional-time rather than the price paid. One honest caveat: I have not read the gate's implementation this pass, because the instructions for this pass name the files I may read and orc/eval/simulate.py is not one of them. My reading is that `sma:<days>` deploys while price is above its <days> average, the complement of `dip:`. If it carries the other sign it is a long-lookback cousin of closed H0007 and should be killed on those grounds; one grep settles it, and I would rather have that stated than discovered.

The abandonment leg is `stop_loss`, which per the reading on the record in configs/killed/H0010.json exits everything and stops depositing when pnl/contributed reaches -x. H0010 proposed that field alone and codex killed it because its claimed payer -- a mandate constraining pnl over cumulative contributions -- is not a constraint anyone actually operates under. That objection does not transfer. The payer here is not a mandate; it is the liquidation engine, whose trigger is the same coordinate the field reads, and the ruin rates it would act on did not exist as measurements when H0010 was reviewed.

Why both legs are in one hypothesis, rather than two. Because the mechanism axis cannot be numeric in this vocabulary. `gate` is a string and the shape diagnostic reads `sma:50` and `sma:200` as unrelated labels, so a gate-only grid is refused mechanically before registration. Of the horizon-neutral numeric fields Track A has, `leverage` is already known to be affine in tm_q05 at this shape (same verdict: "affine in leverage to under 2e-3"), which makes the spike test vacuous, and `take_profit` has no payer here. `stop_loss` is the one numeric axis that is neither vacuous nor payer-less: it is the only field that truncates the measured ruin, so it is honestly the axis I expect to matter for the left tail, and the 3x4 factorial is what lets the composition clause ask whether the two legs do anything together that either does alone.

What is honestly weak. Four symbols, and Track A independence comes from start dates over one history -- H0001 reports between 1.02 and 1.40 independent paths per symbol -- so this is at best four experiments and the report must say four, not the offset count. Nobody pays us in this shape: the best available outcome is a bounded worst case, which is a map entry and not an edge. The best cell on the primary metric is expected at the tightest stop on every symbol whose 5th-percentile path is negative, because a cap caps, and that is arithmetic rather than a finding. And this is a PARTIAL test of the named payer: the panel holds bars, not fills, so it can measure whether the account is taken and at what threshold it stops being taken, but not what the taking COST -- the engine's actual fill, the clearance fee and any auto-deleveraging are outside this data entirely, and the report must not imply otherwise.
proposal.kill_condition:
Notation. Every cell is contribution 100, stride_days 7, n_contributions 52, hold_days 728, leverage 1.0, take_profit null, include_funding true, clock 1h -- a 1092-day programme, KT-1's three-year frame, so funding_frac_q50 here is directly comparable with the 36% KT-1 measured, and all twelve cells share one nominal horizon so PBO is expected to be computable. G is the gate and s the stop. L(G,s) is the recorded liquidation_rate; T05 is tm_q05; T50 is tm_q50; F(G,s) is funding_frac_q50; R05 is the annualised money-weighted return at the 5th percentile of start dates. The universe is four symbols. Every threshold below is frozen now, before any result is seen. The floor 0.05 is chosen because the start-date ensemble carries roughly one independent path per symbol: below 5% of start offsets, ruin is one unlucky window rather than a property of the shape, and this data cannot tell those two apart.

Premise, not a clause. L(none, null) is already measured off-ledger and recorded in configs/killed/H0012.json: BTCUSDT 0.570, ETHUSDT 0.484, BNBUSDT 0.000, DOGEUSDT 0.800. BNBUSDT is therefore the negative control -- a symbol with no ruin to prevent, on which any improvement the gate shows is not ruin-prevention. No clause below asks whether the ruin exists.

Closed if the gate does not act on the ruin. Counting only the three symbols with L(none, null) >= 0.05: if no SMA level brings L(G, null) below half of L(none, null) on at least 2 of those 3, then withholding deployment on a trend state does not identify the stretches that kill the account, the notional-time claim is wrong, and no clause below may be read as rescuing it.

Closed also if the gate is under-deployment in disguise. F is the funding bill per dollar invested, so deploying less capital does not move it while avoiding the expensive stretches does. If no SMA level brings F(G, null) to at most 0.80 x F(none, null) on 3 or more of the 4 symbols, then the gate is shrinking the position rather than selecting periods, and any tail improvement it shows is arithmetic. This clause is evaluable only if the `invested` denominator of the recorded funding_frac counts capital actually deployed; if it counts deposits that were never deployed, the clause is recorded NOT EVALUABLE and may NOT be counted as survived, and the report must state which of the two it is.

Closed also if the gate pays for the rent with the recovery. If T50(G, null) < 0.90 x T50(none, null) for every SMA level on 3 or more of the 4 symbols, then sitting in cash through the bottom costs more in missed recovery than it saves in rent, and the shape trades a measured tax for a larger unmeasured one. The median is used here and not the mean, which section 4 forbids arguing from. If tm_q50 is not a recorded field, this clause is recorded NOT EVALUABLE and may not be counted as survived.

Closed also if the accumulator cannot get in front of the engine. If L(none, 0.15) >= 0.05 on 2 or more of the three symbols with L(none, null) >= 0.05, then even abandoning the programme at a 15% loss on contributed capital does not stop the account being taken -- the loss arrives inside the bar faster than an account-level check can act -- and no threshold available in this vocabulary reaches the payer at all. That sentence is then the finding this family records.

Closed also if the two legs do not compose. If the best (SMA, s) cell's R05 does not exceed BOTH the best (SMA, null) cell and the best (none, s) cell by at least 2 percentage points annualised on 3 or more of the 4 symbols, then this is not one rule shape but two one-field questions welded together, and each has already been refused as one.

Closed also if the reported PBO is at or above 0.5 on a majority of the symbols for which it is computed. All twelve cells share one nominal horizon by construction, so this clause is expected to be evaluable; if PBO comes back uncomputed on all four symbols, the report must record that this family's selection was never tested rather than counting this clause as survived.

Not counted toward any clause above. The best cell on the primary metric is expected at the tightest stop wherever the 5th-percentile path is negative, because a cap caps; neither its value nor its shape diagnostic is evidence for or against this family, and no cell of this grid may be presented anywhere as an accumulation rule worth running on that basis. The diagnostic is nevertheless computable here -- stop_loss carries three numeric levels and the interior level 0.35 has a neighbour on both sides -- and whether it reads PLATEAU or SPIKE is worth recording and changes no clause.

verdict.reason: [claude] 제안이 스스로 건 조건 — "If it carries the other sign it is a long-lookback cousin of closed H0007 and should be killed on those grounds; one grep settles it" — 이 그대로 성립한다: `orc/eval/simulate.py:271` `gate_below_sma`는 "Deploy only when price is under the simple average of the PRIOR window"이고 `out[ok] = close[ok] <= sma[ok]`이므로, `sma:<days>`는 추세 게이트가 아니라 참조점만 trailing peak에서 이동평균으로 바꾼 `dip:`과 동일 부호의 약세 매수 게이트 — 즉 닫힌 H0007의 형태이며, H0009를 죽인 바로 그 re-skin이다. 실제 부호에서는 현금이 상승 구간에 놀고 하락 구간에 배치되므로 "notional-time을 줄여 비싼 구간을 피한다"는 메커니즘 주장과 첫 번째 kill clause(게이트가 ruin에 작용하는지)는 코드에 없는 동작을 대상으로 쓰여 있다. | [codex] The implemented `sma:<days>` gate deploys when price is below its prior-window SMA, not above it; by the proposal’s own stated contingency, this makes H0013 a long-lookback re-skin of the closed H0007 weakness-buying family rather than the claimed trend-state withholding rule.
